title: AI-Based Cognitive Gaming and Memory Assistance Platform for Elderly Dementia Patients in North Eastern Region (NER)
org: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)
department: Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (MDoNER)
description:
Background:
The North Eastern Region (NER) is witnessing a gradual rise in age-related cognitive disorders such as dementia and memory loss among the elderly population. Many families in remote and rural areas face challenges in accessing specialized neurological care, cognitive therapy, and long-term elderly support services due to limited healthcare infrastructure and geographical barriers.
Elderly patients suffering from dementia often experience memory decline, confusion, anxiety, and social isolation, while caregivers face difficulties in continuous monitoring and engagement. There is limited availability of affordable and culturally inclusive digital therapeutic solutions tailored for elderly individuals in the North-Eastern Region.
To strengthen elderly healthcare and improve cognitive well-being, there is a need for an accessible, engaging, and Al-enabled cognitive gaming solution designed specifically for dementia patients in NER.
Description:
This problem statement seeks the development of an AI-powered cognitive gaming and memory assistance platform for elderly dementia patients in the North Eastern Region.
The solution should:
a. Include interactive cognitive games and activities focused on:
• Memory improvement
• Attention and concentration 0 Daily routine recall
• Pattern and object recognition of emotional and mental engagement b. Use AI/ML algorithms to adapt difficulty levels based on patient performance and cognitive condition c. Support multilingual and voice-assisted interaction suitable for elderly users in NER Include culturally familiar themes, visuals, sounds, and regional language support for d. better engagement e. Provide reminders for:
• Medicines
• Hydration
• Daily activities
• Medical appointments.
f. Enable caregivers and healthcare workers to monitor patient progress through dashboards and activity levels g. Work in low-connectivity environments with offline functionality support h. Be accessible through mobile/tablet devices with a simple and elderly-friendly interface The platform should encourage long-term cognitive engagement, emotional well-being, and social interaction among elderly users.
Expected Solution: A user-friendly Al-enabled cognitive assistance platform with:
• Adaptive gaming and memory training modules
• Voice-enabled multilingual interface
• Cognitive performance tracking and analytics dashboard
• Caregiver monitoring and alert system
• Offline synchronization support for remote areas
• Secure patient data management system
• Simple and accessible UI/UX designed for elderly users The solution should support early cognitive intervention, improve quality of life for elderly dementia patients, and strengthen digital healthcare accessibility across the North Eastern Region.
summary: Innovation (4/5): draws on ai, ml applied to a space technology problem, placing it in the breakthrough band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (4/5): reaches a broad public/citizen base within Space Technology. Tech Depth (3/5): centers on infrastructure. Sustainability (4/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (4/5): built to extend across states/users with modest rework. Total 22/30 -> Green verdict.

detail.title: AI-Based Cognitive Gaming and Memory Assistance Platform for Elderly Dementia Patients in North Eastern Region (NER)

overview.in_plain_terms: Build a set of games and memory exercises for elderly dementia patients in NER, ones that adapt to each person and work even where specialist care doesn't reach.
overview.why_it_matters: Families in remote NER villages often have no access to cognitive therapy at all. A well-designed digital tool doesn't replace a neurologist, but it's the difference between some support and none.
pain_points: Limited access to neurological/cognitive care in remote NER areas.
Caregivers struggle with continuous monitoring and engagement.
No culturally-relevant, affordable digital therapeutic options exist for this population.
overview.background: Dementia and memory-loss cases are rising in NER's elderly population, but specialist care is geographically and financially out of reach for many rural families.
overview.whats_being_asked: An AI-adaptive cognitive gaming platform covering memory, attention, routine recall, and pattern recognition, tuned for cultural relevance and accessibility.
expected_solution: Interactive cognitive games targeting memory, attention, recall, and recognition.
Culturally-relevant content for the NER context.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Moderate. Adaptive cognitive gaming exists as a category already, the innovation here is in cultural/regional adaptation and caregiver integration, not a new therapeutic concept.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Medium. Game content + adaptive difficulty logic is achievable in 36 hours; the harder part is making it genuinely elderly-accessible (UX) rather than technically complex.

competitive_landscape.note: Elder-care/cognitive-health PS are less common than generic healthtech pitches this cycle, a reasonably clear lane if executed with real UX care.

innovation.note: Adaptive difficulty and cultural tailoring are real but incremental improvements on an established category.

invention.note: Achievable scope, several game modules plus an adaptation layer, not overly technical.

technical_feasibility.note: No exotic data dependencies, this is buildable end-to-end with content and UX work as the main lift.

impact_and_benefits.note: Fills a genuine care gap for an underserved elderly population with no other access route.

architecture.note: Low integration risk, the real work is game design and elderly-friendly UX, not systems complexity.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with UX/design strength. Feasible in 36 hours, real impact, and a less-crowded lane than most healthtech PS.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Achievable end-to-end in the timeframe without a fragile data pipeline, a rare feature among the NER healthtech PS set.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building 'just games' without genuine elderly-accessibility UX (large text, simple controls, low cognitive load) will read as generic and miss the actual point.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: If nobody on the team has UX/accessibility design experience, this PS's quality bar (elderly-friendly interaction) will be hard to hit convincingly.

idea_0_4: Pick 2-3 game types to build well rather than attempting all four categories shallowly.
Design for elderly users from the first sketch, large touch targets, minimal text, simple navigation.
Decide what 'culturally relevant' means concretely for your content, local imagery, language, familiar objects.
prototype_4_22: Build the core game loop for your chosen 2-3 games.
Build the adaptive-difficulty logic, simple rule-based adjustment is fine, doesn't need to be deep ML.
Start caregiver-facing progress view in parallel.
integration_22_30: Connect games to the adaptive layer and caregiver dashboard.
User-test with a genuinely non-technical person if possible, an elderly relative or simulate the constraint seriously.
Polish accessibility: font size, contrast, audio cues.
polish_30_36: Finalize caregiver dashboard showing engagement/progress trends.
Rehearse a demo that shows the adaptation happening live, difficulty visibly changing based on performance.
Prepare to speak to cultural-relevance choices specifically, judges will probe this.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Demo it on an actual elderly-simulated interaction, oversized buttons, simple flow, and narrate why each UX choice exists, that's more convincing than listing features.

strengths: Fully buildable in 36 hours without fragile data dependencies.
weaknesses: Success depends heavily on UX quality, not just feature completeness.
Risk of reading as generic if cultural/regional tailoring isn't concrete and visible.

roles_needed: Backend for adaptive logic + caregiver view
team_fit.ideal_ratio: Weight toward design/UX, this PS is won or lost on interaction quality, not backend complexity.
team_fit.approach: Start with paper prototypes of the game flow before writing code, elderly-accessible UX needs iteration.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: Game logic scaffolding and the adaptive-difficulty rule engine, standard patterns.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: What actually makes an interface usable for someone with cognitive decline, and what content is genuinely culturally relevant to NER, not generic 'Indian' content.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: AI-generated generic game content won't read as culturally specific, and a judge from the region will notice immediately.

data_resource_availability.status: No external dataset dependency, this is a self-contained build.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not applicable, main resourcing need is design/content time, not data.

judge_qna.question: What makes this culturally relevant to NER specifically, versus a generic elderly cognitive game?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Point to specific content choices, local imagery, familiar routines, language options, made deliberately, not just a labeling change.
judge_qna.follow_up: Did you validate any of this with someone actually from the region?

judge_qna.question: How do you know the adaptive difficulty is actually helping, not just changing?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Describe the metric you're adapting on (response time, accuracy) and what direction of adjustment counts as 'helping' versus just reactive noise.
judge_qna.follow_up: What happens if a patient's performance is inconsistent day to day?
